1: //! # Unset Variables Engine
2: //!
3: //! This module implements file-level checks for variables that might not be
4: //! defined before use. It wraps 6 related MATLAB Code Analyzer checks into a
5: //! single rule engine that leverages the symbol table and definite-assignment
6: //! analysis.
7: //!
8: //! ## Checks
9: //!
10: //! | ID | Description |
11: //! |----|-------------|
12: //! | NODEF | Variable might not be defined before use |
13: //! | USENS | Variable used but might not be set in all code paths |
14: //! | PSET | Variable set in one branch but not others |
15: //! | SUSENS | Script variable used before set |
16: //! | SVNODEF | Variable in script might not be defined |
17: //! | STOUT | Output variable might not be assigned |
18: //!
19: //! ## Configuration
20: //!
21: //! ```toml
22: //! [lint.rules.UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE]
23: //! severity = "warning"
24: //! ignore = ["myGlobalWorkspaceVar"]
25: //! ```
26:

29: use mlt_core::{Category, Config, Diagnostic, FileContext, Rule, Severity};
30: use serde::Deserialize;
31: use tree_sitter::{Node, Tree};

34: use crate::analysis::symbols::{DefKind, ScopeKind, SymbolTable};

37: // Constants
38: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

40: /// Common MATLAB builtins that look like variables but are actually
41: /// constants/functions and should not trigger unset-variable warnings.
42: const MATLAB_BUILTINS: &[&str] = &[
43:     "true", "false", "pi", "inf", "Inf", "nan", "NaN", "eps", "i", "j", "end", "nargin",
44:     "nargout", "varargin", "varargout", "ans",
45: ];
46:

48: // Rule-specific configuration
49: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

51: /// Configuration for the unset-variables engine.
52: ///
53: /// Deserialized from `[lint.rules.UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE]` in `.mlt.toml`.
54: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
55: pub struct UnsetVariablesConfig {
56:     /// Variable names to ignore (e.g., common workspace variables).
57:     #[serde(default)]
58:     pub ignore: Vec<String>,
59: }

65: /// File-level rule engine that detects variables that might not be defined
66: /// before use. Emits diagnostics under multiple check IDs depending on context.
67: pub struct UnsetVariablesEngine {
68:     /// Rule-specific configuration (retained for future use / serialization).
69:     _config: UnsetVariablesConfig,
70:     /// Precomputed set of ignored names (builtins + user-configured).
71:     ignore_set: HashSet<String>,
72: }
73: 
74: impl UnsetVariablesEngine {
75:     /// Factory constructor — reads rule-specific params from config.
76:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
77:         let rule_config: UnsetVariablesConfig = config.rule_params("UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE");
78:         let mut ignore_set: HashSet<String> =
79:             MATLAB_BUILTINS.iter().map(|s| (*s).to_string()).collect();
80:         for name in &rule_config.ignore {
81:             ignore_set.insert(name.clone());
82:         }
83:         Box::new(Self {
84:             _config: rule_config,
85:             ignore_set,
86:         })
87:     }
88: 
89:     /// Check whether a variable name should be ignored.
90:     fn is_ignored(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
91:         self.ignore_set.contains(name)
92:     }
93: 
94:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
95:     // Function scope checks
96:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
97: 
98:     /// Run definite-assignment analysis on function scopes and emit diagnostics.
99:     fn check_function_scopes(
100:         &self,
101:         tree: &Tree,
102:         source: &str,
103:         symbol_table: &SymbolTable,
104:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
105:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
106: 
107:         for scope in &symbol_table.scopes {
108:             // Only process function-like scopes.
109:             if !matches!(
110:                 scope.kind,
111:                 ScopeKind::Function
112:                     | ScopeKind::LocalFunction
113:                     | ScopeKind::NestedFunction
114:                     | ScopeKind::Method
115:             ) {
116:                 continue;
117:             }
118: 
119:             // Find the corresponding function_definition node.
120:             let Some(func_node) = find_function_node_at(tree, &scope.byte_range) else {
121:                 continue;
122:             };
123: 
124:             // Run definite-assignment analysis.
125:             let da = analyze_definite_assignment(func_node, source);
126: 
127:             // Emit NODEF/USENS for possibly-unset variables.
128:             self.emit_possibly_unset_diagnostics(&da, &mut diagnostics);
129: 
130:             // Check output arguments: STOUT.
131:             self.check_output_args(scope, &da, &mut diagnostics);
132:         }
133: 
134:         diagnostics
135:     }
136: 
137:     /// Emit diagnostics for possibly-unset variables from definite-assignment results.
138:     fn emit_possibly_unset_diagnostics(
139:         &self,
140:         da: &DefiniteAssignment,
141:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
142:     ) {
143:         // Track which variable names have already been reported to avoid duplicates.
144:         let mut reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
145: 
146:         for unset_var in &da.possibly_unset {
147:             if self.is_ignored(&unset_var.name) {
148:                 continue;
149:             }
150:             if reported.contains(&unset_var.name) {
151:                 continue;
152:             }
153:             reported.insert(unset_var.name.clone());
154: 
155:             // If the variable is in the definitely-assigned set at function end
156:             // but was used before that point, it's USENS (used but not set in
157:             // all paths). Otherwise it's NODEF (never defined at all on some paths).
158:             let (rule_id, message) = if da.definitely_assigned.contains(&unset_var.name) {
159:                 (
160:                     "USENS",
161:                     format!(
162:                         "Variable '{}' might not be set in all code paths before this use",
163:                         unset_var.name
164:                     ),
165:                 )
166:             } else {
167:                 (
168:                     "NODEF",
169:                     format!(
170:                         "Variable '{}' might not be defined before this use",
171:                         unset_var.name
172:                     ),
173:                 )
174:             };
175: 
176:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
177:                 rule_id,
178:                 message,
179:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
180:                 byte_range: unset_var.use_byte_range.clone(),
181:                 line: unset_var.use_line,
182:                 column: unset_var.use_column,
183:                 fix: None,
184:             });
185:         }
186:     }
187: 
188:     /// Check that all output arguments are definitely assigned (STOUT).
189:     fn check_output_args(
190:         &self,
191:         scope: &crate::analysis::symbols::Scope,
192:         _da: &DefiniteAssignment,
193:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
194:     ) {
195:         for def in &scope.defs {
196:             if def.kind != DefKind::OutputArg {
197:                 continue;
198:             }
199:             if self.is_ignored(&def.name) {
200:                 continue;
201:             }
202: 
203:             // Check if the output variable is definitely assigned at function end.
204:             // The output arg name is pre-added to the assigned set by
205:             // collect_function_args, so we need to check if there is an actual
206:             // assignment (not just the output declaration itself). We look for
207:             // any Assignment-kind def in the scope for this variable name.
208:             let has_assignment = scope
209:                 .defs
210:                 .iter()
211:                 .any(|d| d.name == def.name && d.kind == DefKind::Assignment);
212: 
213:             // If there's no assignment and the name is not in the definitely-
214:             // assigned set from the analysis (excluding the initial output arg
215:             // declaration), emit STOUT.
216:             if !has_assignment && !self.has_non_output_def(scope, &def.name) {
217:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
218:                     rule_id: "STOUT",
219:                     message: format!(
220:                         "Output variable '{}' might not be assigned in function '{}'",
221:                         def.name, scope.name
222:                     ),
223:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
224:                     byte_range: def.byte_range.clone(),
225:                     line: def.line,
226:                     column: def.column,
227:                     fix: None,
228:                 });
229:             }
230:         }
231:     }
232: 
233:     /// Check whether a variable has any non-OutputArg definition in the scope.
234:     fn has_non_output_def(
235:         &self,
236:         scope: &crate::analysis::symbols::Scope,
237:         name: &str,
238:     ) -> bool {
239:         scope
240:             .defs
241:             .iter()
242:             .any(|d| d.name == name && d.kind != DefKind::OutputArg)
243:     }

246:     // Script scope checks
247:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

249:     /// Check script scopes for variables used before being set.
250:     fn check_script_scopes(&self, symbol_table: &SymbolTable) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
251:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
252: 
253:         for scope in &symbol_table.scopes {
254:             if scope.kind != ScopeKind::Script {
255:                 continue;
256:             }
257: 
258:             // In scripts, variables must be defined before use within the file.
259:             // We check for uses that appear before any definition.
260:             let mut reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
261: 
262:             for var_use in &scope.uses {
263:                 if self.is_ignored(&var_use.name) {
264:                     continue;
265:                 }
266:                 if reported.contains(&var_use.name) {
267:                     continue;
268:                 }
269: 
270:                 // Find the earliest definition of this variable in the scope.
271:                 let earliest_def = scope
272:                     .defs
273:                     .iter()
274:                     .filter(|d| d.name == var_use.name)
275:                     .min_by_key(|d| d.byte_range.start);
276: 
277:                 match earliest_def {
278:                     None => {
279:                         // Variable is used but never defined in the script → SVNODEF.
280:                         reported.insert(var_use.name.clone());
281:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
282:                             rule_id: "SVNODEF",
283:                             message: format!(
284:                                 "Variable '{}' in script might not be defined",
285:                                 var_use.name
286:                             ),
287:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
288:                             byte_range: var_use.byte_range.clone(),
289:                             line: var_use.line,
290:                             column: var_use.column,
291:                             fix: None,
292:                         });
293:                     }
294:                     Some(def) if var_use.byte_range.start < def.byte_range.start => {
295:                         // Variable is used before its first definition → SUSENS.
296:                         reported.insert(var_use.name.clone());
297:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
298:                             rule_id: "SUSENS",
299:                             message: format!(
300:                                 "Script variable '{}' is used before it is set",
301:                                 var_use.name
302:                             ),
303:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
304:                             byte_range: var_use.byte_range.clone(),
305:                             line: var_use.line,
306:                             column: var_use.column,
307:                             fix: None,
308:                         });
309:                     }
310:                     _ => {
311:                         // Variable is used after being defined — OK.
312:                     }
313:                 }
314:             }
315:         }
316: 
317:         diagnostics
318:     }
319: 
320:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
321:     // PSET: partial-branch assignment check
322:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
323: 
324:     /// Check for variables set in some branches of if/switch but not all (PSET).
325:     ///
326:     /// This check walks `if_statement` and `switch_statement` nodes looking for
327:     /// variables that are assigned in some branches but not others.
328:     fn check_partial_branch_assignment(
329:         &self,
330:         tree: &Tree,
331:         source: &str,
332:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
333:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
334:         self.walk_pset(tree.root_node(), source, &mut diagnostics);
335:         diagnostics
336:     }

338:     /// DFS walk to find if/switch statements for PSET analysis.
339:     fn walk_pset(
340:         &self,
341:         node: Node,
342:         source: &str,
343:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
344:     ) {
345:         match node.kind() {
346:             "if_statement" => {
347:                 self.check_if_pset(node, source, diagnostics);
348:             }
349:             "switch_statement" => {
350:                 self.check_switch_pset(node, source, diagnostics);
351:             }
352:             _ => {}
353:         }
354: 
355:         // Recurse into children.
356:         let count = node.child_count();
357:         for i in 0..count {
358:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
359:                 self.walk_pset(child, source, diagnostics);
360:             }
361:         }
362:     }

364:     /// Check an if_statement for partial assignment (PSET).
365:     fn check_if_pset(
366:         &self,
367:         node: Node,
368:         source: &str,
369:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
370:     ) {
371:         let mut branch_assignments: Vec<HashSet<String>> = Vec::new();
372:         let mut has_else = false;
373: 
374:         let count = node.child_count();
375:         for i in 0..count {
376:             let Some(child) = node.child(i) else {
377:                 continue;
378:             };
379:             match child.kind() {
380:                 "block" => {
381:                     // The main if-body block.
382:                     branch_assignments.push(collect_block_assignments(child, source));
383:                 }
384:                 "elseif_clause" => {
385:                     let inner_count = child.child_count();
386:                     for j in 0..inner_count {
387:                         if let Some(inner) = child.child(j) {
388:                             if inner.kind() == "block" {
389:                                 branch_assignments
390:                                     .push(collect_block_assignments(inner, source));
391:                                 break;
392:                             }
393:                         }
394:                     }
395:                 }
396:                 "else_clause" => {
397:                     has_else = true;
398:                     let inner_count = child.child_count();
399:                     for j in 0..inner_count {
400:                         if let Some(inner) = child.child(j) {
401:                             if inner.kind() == "block" {
402:                                 branch_assignments
403:                                     .push(collect_block_assignments(inner, source));
404:                                 break;
405:                             }
406:                         }
407:                     }
408:                 }
409:                 _ => {}
410:             }
411:         }
412: 
413:         // Only emit PSET if there's an else branch (complete coverage).
414:         if !has_else || branch_assignments.len() < 2 {
415:             return;
416:         }
417: 
418:         // Find variables assigned in some branches but not all.
419:         let all_vars: HashSet<String> = branch_assignments
420:             .iter()
421:             .flat_map(|s| s.iter().cloned())
422:             .collect();

424:         for var_name in &all_vars {

438:                         severity: Severity::Warning,

528:     /// Find the location of the first assignment to a variable within a compound
529:     /// statement (for PSET diagnostic positioning).
530:     fn find_assignment_location(
531:         &self,
532:         node: Node,
533:         source: &str,
534:         var_name: &str,
535:     ) -> Option<(std::ops::Range<usize>, usize, usize)> {
536:         // DFS search for the first assignment to var_name.
537:         let mut stack = vec![node];
538:         while let Some(current) = stack.pop() {
539:             if current.kind() == "assignment" {
540:                 if let Some(lhs) = current.child_by_field_name("left") {
541:                     if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
542:                         let name = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
543:                         if name == var_name {
544:                             let pos = lhs.start_position();
545:                             return Some((
546:                                 lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte(),
547:                                 pos.row + 1,
548:                                 pos.column + 1,
549:                             ));
550:                         }
551:                     }
552:                 }
553:             }
554:             // Push children in reverse so we visit left-to-right.
555:             let count = current.child_count();
556:             for i in (0..count).rev() {
557:                 if let Some(child) = current.child(i) {
558:                     stack.push(child);
559:                 }
560:             }
561:         }
562:         None
563:     }
564: }

622: /// Find a `function_definition` node in the tree that matches the given byte range.
623: ///
624: /// Performs a DFS from the root, returning the first `function_definition` node
625: /// whose byte range matches.
626: fn find_function_node_at<'a>(tree: &'a Tree, byte_range: &std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
627:     let mut stack = vec![tree.root_node()];
628:     while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
629:         if node.kind() == "function_definition"
630:             && node.start_byte() == byte_range.start
631:             && node.end_byte() == byte_range.end
632:         {
633:             return Some(node);
634:         }
635:         // Only recurse into nodes that overlap with the target range.
636:         let count = node.child_count();
637:         for i in (0..count).rev() {
638:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
639:                 if child.start_byte() <= byte_range.end && child.end_byte() >= byte_range.start {
640:                     stack.push(child);
641:                 }
642:             }
643:         }
644:     }
645:     None
646: }
647: 
648: /// Collect all variable names assigned in a block (shallow — only direct
649: /// assignment statements, not nested blocks).
650: fn collect_block_assignments(block: Node, source: &str) -> HashSet<String> {
651:     let mut assigned = HashSet::new();
652:     let count = block.child_count();
653:     for i in 0..count {
654:         let Some(child) = block.child(i) else {
655:             continue;
656:         };
657:         if child.kind() == "assignment" {
658:             if let Some(lhs) = child.child_by_field_name("left") {
659:                 match lhs.kind() {
660:                     "identifier" => {
661:                         let name = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
662:                         assigned.insert(name.to_string());
663:                     }
664:                     "multioutput_variable" => {
665:                         let lhs_count = lhs.child_count();
666:                         for j in 0..lhs_count {
667:                             if let Some(id) = lhs.child(j) {
668:                                 if id.kind() == "identifier" {
669:                                     let name = &source[id.start_byte()..id.end_byte()];
670:                                     assigned.insert(name.to_string());
671:                                 }
672:                             }
673:                         }
674:                     }
675:                     _ => {}
676:                 }
677:             }
678:         }
679:     }
680:     assigned
681: }
